subject: Post-demo follow-up: input/output retention matrix and masking playbook

Subject: Post-demo follow-up: input/output retention matrix and masking playbook

Hi Samir — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on around how Redwood treats customer inputs and the derived outputs: 

What we covered (high level):
- Inputs (raw prompts/query payloads): by default not persisted beyond request lifetime unless customer enables logging or a debug trace.
- Derived outputs (model-generated text, classifications, embeddings): options for ephemeral-only (never stored), short-term TTL (configured per-session or per-route), or persisted for analytics with explicit retention periods.
- Logging controls: token-level logs are gated — can be disabled or routed to a customer-managed storage endpoint for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Data residency: hosted region controls for where persisted artifacts live; Dedicated/Private supports on-prem/VPC.

Attached: retention-matrix.xlsx (summary matrix mapping types -> default retention -> configurable TTLs) and audit-evidence-overview.pdf (what we can provide for SOC2-style requests).

Open questions / agreed follow-ups from today:
1) You asked for a short, concrete mapping for: prompts vs. outputs vs. metadata (who touched it, timestamps, model version) — attached matrix covers that; please flag anything missing.
2) Confirm whether Acuvera needs ephemeral-only behavior for any routes (e.g., PHI redaction use-cases) — if yes, we can propose a routing rule with TTL=0.
3) Evidence: you requested sample logging schema and an example export of audit logs — we can provide a redacted sample (aditya will attach).

Next steps:
- Aditya will send the technical note and a redacted sample audit export (ETA: next 2 business days).
- Lauren will prepare a short one-pager on compliance fit (limiting where things are persisted and encryption in transit/at rest).
- I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security team next week if that works (proposed times attached in the Drive link).

Thanks — if anything above is off, call it out and I’ll correct.

Best,
Maya

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 15:44 Samir Patel <samir.patel@acuverahealth.com> wrote:
> 1) For route-level TTLs, what are the enforcement guarantees? If TTL=0 (ephemeral), do you ensure (a) no disk write on your hosted control plane, and (b) no backups include that data?

Short answer: TTL enforcement is at the routing layer and backed by the storage policy. For hosted Redis/KV caches we mark keys tenant-ephemeral and set immediate expiry; for outputs we can operate in a passthrough mode where no persistent write occurs on Redwood-managed object stores.
- (a) For ephemeral routes on Hosted: runtime avoids persisting payloads to object storage; short-lived in-memory and ephemeral cache only. Our control plane metadata (route id and counters) are recorded for billing/telemetry but are configurable (see below).
- (b) Backups: ephemeral-marked objects are excluded from scheduled backups; we maintain a manifest and backup-exclusion policy audited in our SOC2 scope.

> 2) When you say "metadata" (model version, timestamps, route id) — do you persist any of that by default for monitoring? If so, can that be redacted or minimized?

By default we persist minimal monitoring metadata: timestamps, anonymized route id (hashed), model family & semantic version (not full weights), and latency counters. We do not store raw prompt text in that monitoring footprint by default. Customers can opt-out of metadata collection or choose to route logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS endpoint for Dedicated/Private.

> 3) Does Redwood provide a verifiable deletion/expunge report (hashes/manifest) for persisted outputs when requested?

Yes for Dedicated & Private: we provide deletion manifests (object keys + deletion timestamp) and optional HMAC-signed manifests for proof of deletion. For Hosted customers, we offer deletion summaries and can provide export/manifests for persisted outputs within contractual commitments; for regulatory/enterprise cases we recommend Dedicated/Private for highest provable controls.

Attached: sample-audit-log-schema.json (redacted) — contains field names and sample values with PHI removed. Also included a short note on routing flags you can toggle via the API.

If it helps, we can prepare a short SR on the guarantees and include the backup-exclusion excerpt from our SOC2 evidence pack.

— Aditya
